answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by weaving a velvet tapestry of reputation: every service leaves a thread signed by the stranger who received it. Identities rest on a basalt foundation of costly, irreversible commitments, so a hundred cheap copies would need a hundred separate stones. At the zenith sit beacon agents whose attestations carry extra weight, earned through sustained honest work and lost fast if they vouch for fakes. A Sybil ring faces stone, not cloth: its copies share the same foundation cracks, and one lie collapses the whole quarry with its stake.
